gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-poppins: Expressive letters spread out like beads on a long thread make Bruno Ace SC feel unmistakable up top, with no thinning anywhere. Poppins is the plain sans that keeps things sturdy.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab fills the middle of each line with open, sturdy letters and a precise, structured feel. Bruno Ace SC above it stays unvarying and wide, and that tension is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-cal-sans-fs-karma: Karma brings a trustworthy, classic serif texture, with caps and lowercase sitting close in height and terminals that finish clear of the stem. Cal Sans above it is inflated and smooth, so the two feel like round glass against quiet ink.
gen-gf-cambo-archivo: Archivo has a commanding x-height and curves that open outward instead of curling in, so it reads with confident clarity. And Cambo's measured swell from hairline to stem gives the heading a traditional, editorial voice above it.
gen-gf-cambo-fs-asap: Cambo's small letters look thick with height, like bundled cable, and its brush-stroke shapes vary only slightly in pressure. Asap follows in sans-serif, its body height nearly matching the capitals.
gen-gf-cambo-fs-epilogue: Bundled-cable lowercase and a soft brush stroke give Cambo its traditional, editorial look, while Epilogue underneath is curvy and wire-thin. Its quiet, level beat carries a page without a single accent of weight.
gen-gf-cambo-fs-fira-sans: Cambo wears a traditional, editorial face, with mid-level stroke contrast and a gentle brush-stroke feel in each letter. Fira Sans has a larger-than-usual x-height and no shift from heavy to light, which is the sharpest difference in the pair.
gen-gf-cambo-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase body and broad open counters, so it feels professional and trustworthy on sight. Cambo carries the heading with weight that stretches only slightly, like rubber cord, giving it a traditional, editorial lead.
gen-gf-cambo-fs-supreme: Supreme reads as a thick, heavy strip of text through the middle, with letters held open rather than curled shut. Over a longer passage it stays crisp, while Cambo's mild thick-and-thin rhythm gives the heading its edge.
